Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The players are out in the middle now. Kyle Mayers and Brandon King are the two openers for West Indies. Hardik Pandya to start proceedings with the ball.
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, India have posted a respectable total, but they need their bowlers to be on point right from the start and make early inroads to put pressure on the batters. West Indies have a long batting line-up and they will be confident of gunning this total down, but they also need to bat a bit sensibly. Joins us in a bit to see how the chase unfolds and which team wins this series.

West Indies, on the other hand, were hot and cold with their bowling effort. Akeal Hosein gave them a perfect by getting rid of both Shubman Gill and Yashasvi Jaiswal pretty quickly. However, Alzarri Joseph proved to be very expensive and they let India get back in the game. Roston Chase then broke the partnership with a terrific diving catch to dismiss Tilak Varma while Romario Shepherd followed it up with two wickets as well. They were brilliant at the death and use the two rain-breaks to their advantage to break the momentum of India. Shephard ended up with four wickets while Jason Holder also chipped in with a couple in the end.

The Indian openers failed to continue their good form and were back in the hut inside the first two overs. It was the 49-run stand between Suryakumar Yadav and Tilak Varma that steadied things and brought back control for them. SKY lost a few partners at the other end but that didn't bother him much as he registered another fantastic fifty. Sanju Samson failed to grab his opportunity and Hardik Pandya struggled as well, but along with that knock from SKY, a few lusty blows from Axar Patel, and a last-ball boundary from Mukesh Kumar got them over the 160-run mark.

A good battle between bat and ball comes to an end! West Indies have restricted India to 165/9! The pendulum swung both ways with Windies picking up wickets at regular intervals courtesy of a fine spell from Romario Shepherd, but Suryakumar Yadav fought a lone battle for the visitors with a gritty half-century which helped them to get to this total.

FOUR! Edged away and that will do nicely for Mukesh Kumar and India. Back of a length around off, Kumar has a wild swing across the line but gets a thick outside edge well past the keeper and the ball runs away into the third man fence. 16 runs come off the final over and India finish with 165/9!

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to start! The umpires are out in the middle and so are the players of West Indies. It will be the pair of Yashasvi Jaiswal and Shubman Gill to open the innings for India. Akeal Hosein has been handed the new ball and will get proceedings underway with his left-arm spin. Let's play...

Rovman Powell, the skipper of West Indies says that they are happy to bowl first. Adds that both teams have played good cricket and he is confident in his team to chase down any target. Tells that the bowlers need to stick to the plans for different batters. Informs that there are two changes as Alzarri Joseph is back in for Obed McCoy and Roston Chase replaces Odean Smith.

Hardik Pandya, the captain of India says that they will bat first as it looks like a good track and they have been good with chasing, so, want to challenge themselves. Adds that the track in the last game played really well and they did well to take wickets in the Powerplay. Mentions that on these kinds of wickets, you need to be courageous and even if you get hit, a comeback is always on the cards. Informs that they are going with the same team.

West Indies (Playing XI) - Kyle Mayers, Brandon King, Shai Hope, Nicholas Pooran (WK), Rovman Powell (C), Shimron Hetmyer, Roston Chase (In place of Odean Smith), Jason Holder, Romario Shepherd, Akeal Hosein, Alzarri Joseph (In for Obed McCoy).

India (Unchanged Playing XI) - Shubman Gill, Yashasvi Jaiswal, Suryakumar Yadav, Tilak Varma, Hardik Pandya (C), Sanju Samson(WK), Axar Patel, Arshdeep Singh, Kuldeep Yadav, Yuzvendra Chahal, Mukesh Kumar.
TOSS - Hardik Pandya finally calls it correctly and India have elected to BAT first.

India, on the other hand, have the momentum on their side, and they cruised to a win in the last game. Shubman Gill was back to his best and found his form and Yashasvi Jaiswal scored his maiden fifty in this format as well. They are proving to be a formidable opening partnership. India have Suryakumar Yadav, Hardik Pandya and Tilak Varma who has been brilliant in this series which makes a strong middle order. Arshdeep Singh and Mukesh Kumar are being developed as fine death bowlers and they can handle the Powerplay as well. However, their best bowler has been Kuldeep Yadav who once again picked two wickets in one over in the last game, but Yuzvendra Chahal and Axar Patel need to improve and support him well. They have a lot of quality and will be confident of making it three wins in a row to seal the series. Will they be able to do it? Or Will West Indies snatch it and lift the trophy? An exciting final T20I is coming up shortly. Toss and team news in a bit.

West Indies won the first two matches but after that their performance dropped massively. The main reason is their lackluster bowling attack. Kyle Mayers and Brandon King will look to give them a brisk start but once again the key for them will be Nicholas Pooran. Even though he failed in the last game, he is in good form and Rovman Powell also needs to take more responsibility. Shai Hope came in for Johnson Charles and looked in good touch and they need that stability in their batting. Shimron Hetmyer will also be high on confidence after an excellent fifty in the last match. Alzarri Joseph could be back as he is their most important bowler. Akeal Hosein has been economical but they need him or someone like Jason Holder or Romario Shepherd to pick up wickets in the middle. They will hope that everyone chips in and they get that all-important win.

Hello and a warm welcome folks! An inspiring comeback by the young Indian side from 2-0 to 2-2 has taken this five-match T20I series to the decider which is not that far away now. West Indies had the perfect chance to get a series win over the visitors, but they stumbled at the wrong time and now it is everything to play for at Lauderhill in Florida.
... MATCH DAY ...

It's going to be a quick turnaround as India get ready to continue their winning march and cap off their successful tour of the Caribbean Island and the United States. It is the last and final T20I in this 5-match series which will be played at the Central Broward Regional Park Stadium Turf Ground in Lauderhill, Florida and what excitement we have witnessed so far! India have come roaring back in the series after two disappointing losses and it is all level as we get into the decider. They have now registered two commanding wins with their previous fixture proving to be pretty one-sided as they romped home to a 9-wicket win with 18 balls to spare. They will be mighty pleased to see their openers hit good form as both Yashasvi Jaiswal and Shubman Gill notched up half-centuries and added 165 runs for the opening wicket in 94 deliveries. Suryakumar Yadav and Tilak Varma have already played crucial knocks and they suddenly look like a formidable batting line-up. Arshdeep Singh managed to find his groove as well, as he claimed 3 wickets in the last game. Axar Patel has been hardly used but Yuzvendra Chahal and Kuldeep Yadav have played a massive role in restricting the West Indies batters. The hosts made wholesale changes to their playing eleven but kept their batting order similar only including Shai Hope in place of Johnson Charles. He justified his selection with a well-made half-century but the lack of runs from the in-form batters, Nicholas Pooran and Rovman Powell cost them several runs. They will be hoping Brandon King and Kyle Mayers can get them off to a good start in the final game as it has been long overdue. Obed McCoy, Jason Holder and Odean Smith were brought into the side but none of them were able to put in a decent bowling performance. The load has fallen heavily on Akeal Hosein as the lone spinner with Roston Chase missing out and the management may consider bringing him back for the last game. Will they be able to end this losing streak and clinch the series? Or will India make it three wins in a row and seal the T20I series as well? We will find out soon.
